dedupe_keys.name: sic2 simulation and integration of control for canals

description: SIC² (Simulation and Integration of Control for Canals) is hydraulic simulation software for flows in irrigation canals, rivers and sewage systems. It lets users design and manage a network of canals or rivers through a graphical interface, computes one-dimensional steady and unsteady flow from the Saint-Venant equations, and includes a library of hydraulic devices such as weirs, gates and hydro-mechanical gates and a library of automatic control algorithms for testing regulation of control structures under unsteady flow; a water quality module and a batch mode for control from other programs are documented. It is developed by the G-EAU research unit of INRAE (the tool originated at Cemagref in the late 1980s as a decision support tool for canal managers). Coverage is generic: any canal or river network described by its geometry and devices; geometry can be imported from a terrain model, a survey or a MIKE 11 file. Access: a licence bought from INRAE UMR G-EAU, 14,000 euros for the professional version or 1,000 euros for the teaching and research version, with a year of free corrective maintenance and updates, as listed on the commercial page on 26 September 2026; documentation (user guide, tutorials, theory) is free online. Caveats: proprietary, one-dimensional only, and some pages are in French only. Simulation uses: network flow in irrigation canals, design and optimisation of automatic gate control, and capacity planning of canal systems. Related records: HEC-RAS (model-hec-ras) covers similar one-dimensional unsteady river hydraulics.
